# Whatever It Takes: How WIT Athletics Turned a Bold Vision Into a Community-First Business


*Landmark National Bank Customer Champions Series*


Starting a business takes vision. Building one from the ground up takes persistence, patience, and a willingness to do Whatever It Takes.


For John and Kaycie Bogner, founders of WIT Athletics in Dodge City, Kansas, those words are more than a motivational phrase. They’re the foundation of their business.


What began as a saying on a college football field eventually became the driving force behind a new chapter in entrepreneurship, one that transformed a former bowling alley into a fitness and wellness destination designed around the needs of its community.


With support from family, local business partners, and Landmark National Bank, the Bogners brought their vision to life, learning valuable lessons about taking risks, navigating financial decisions, working together, and building a business centered on community.


## From a Family Business to a New Beginning


Entrepreneurship has always been part of John’s life.


His grandfather founded a beverage distribution business in Dodge City more than 60 years ago. John eventually joined his father in the family business, expecting to spend his career there.


Following his father’s passing in 2015, John continued running the business for the family. But after navigating industry changes and shifting corporate priorities, he began considering a different future.


In September 2022, the family sold the business, opening the door to an entirely new opportunity.


For John, the inspiration had been there for decades.


While playing football at Benedictine College, his team adopted a motto during his junior and senior years: “Whatever It Takes.”


The phrase represented a commitment to doing everything necessary to succeed, whether that meant preparing for practice, staying focused academically, or supporting teammates.


“I’ve followed that motto for 25+ years,” John shared.


But to John, those words carry a much deeper meaning than simply working hard.


In his own definition, doing Whatever It Takes represents an unwavering commitment to achieving a goal, even when the path forward involves obstacles, uncertainty, or sacrifice.


As John explains:


“Doing Whatever It Takes captures an unyielding determination to achieve a goal, no matter the obstacles or sacrifices involved. It’s a mindset that embraces perseverance, responsibility, intensity, and commitment, everyday!”


That mindset also means being willing to push beyond comfort zones, take risks, make difficult decisions, and persevere through challenges rather than giving up when things become difficult.


It’s a philosophy that has guided John for more than two decades, and one that would eventually shape his next business venture.


Years later, those three words became WIT Athletics.


Having spent much of his life involved in fitness, John recognized an opportunity to bring something different to Dodge City. He envisioned a comprehensive athletic facility that offered more than traditional gym equipment, creating a place where individuals and families could pursue healthier lifestyles.


For business owners, John’s journey offers an important perspective: A new venture doesn’t always require an entirely new passion. Sometimes, the strongest business opportunities come from combining years of experience with an unmet need in your community.


## Turning an Ambitious Vision Into a Business Plan


In April 2023, John and Kaycie purchased a former bowling alley that had remained closed since the COVID-19 pandemic.


Transforming the property was no small undertaking.


The family spent approximately nine months removing the bowling lanes, equipment, and existing interior features before moving into the construction and design process.


Even with a clear vision, the project required difficult financial decisions.


Their initial design exceeded the available budget, forcing them to reconsider certain elements and identify ways to bring the project within a realistic financial framework.


Rather than abandoning the concept, they adjusted their approach.


John also sought proposals from three banks as he developed the financing strategy for the new business. Ultimately, he chose Landmark National Bank, where he had established local relationships and found the guidance needed to navigate the project’s complexities.


Building the business plan required careful attention to projections, funding allocations, and financing arrangements, including a Small Business Administration (SBA) loan.


“Building a business plan is difficult. It’s challenging,” John explained. “You’ve got to get the numbers right.”


Throughout the process, John worked closely with Landmark’s Michael Burns to evaluate questions, address challenges, and determine how different funding sources could support the project.


“There were many times I would call, text or email, and Michael would get on it right away, and we would have the answers,” John shared. “I could call him right now, he’d pick up, and we would figure it out.”


For John, having a responsive banking partner who understood his vision made an important difference during a complex process.


For entrepreneurs, WIT’s experience reinforces an important principle: A strong business plan isn’t necessarily one that never changes. It’s one that can adapt to financial realities while protecting the core vision. Having a knowledgeable financial partner to help navigate those adjustments can be just as important as the initial financing itself.


After approximately 12 months of construction, WIT Athletics officially opened on January 17, 2025.


## Building Around the Customer, Not Just the Concept


From the beginning, John and Kaycie wanted WIT Athletics to address barriers that often prevent people from prioritizing fitness.


For some, that barrier is finding time away from their children. For others, it’s feeling uncomfortable or intimidated in a traditional gym environment.


The Bogners approached those challenges as opportunities to create something more inclusive.


One of their priorities was an interactive Kids Club, offering supervised activities for children from six months through 11 years old while parents use the facility.


They also developed a wellness area offering additional services, including saunas, frost lockers, tanning, spray tanning, and red light therapy.


But some of the most meaningful features came from Kaycie’s perspective.


Unlike John, who has always felt comfortable in athletic environments, Kaycie understands how intimidating a gym can feel for someone who doesn’t naturally enjoy working out.


That experience influenced the facility’s layout, including cardio equipment positioned to offer greater privacy and separate workout areas that accommodate different comfort levels.


It also led to one of WIT’s popular offerings: bungee fitness.


Initially, John wasn’t convinced by Kaycie’s suggestion to introduce bungee classes. But she continued advocating for the idea, and eventually the two traveled to Oklahoma City to become certified instructors.


Today, John describes bungee fitness as one of the facility’s most requested classes, and he gives all the credit to Kaycie.


The experience offered an important lesson about partnership and leadership.


John acknowledged that he tends to see the big picture, while Kaycie notices the smaller details that shape a customer’s experience.


Over time, learning to appreciate those differences helped them strengthen both their working relationship and their business.


For business owners, the takeaway is simple: The perspectives that challenge your assumptions may be the very ones that help your business stand apart.


## The Reality of Building a Business Together


While WIT Athletics represents an exciting new chapter, John and Kaycie are candid about the challenges they faced along the way.


Transitioning from an established family business into a startup meant leaving behind predictable schedules and familiar routines.


Some days involved six hours of work, while others stretched to more than 18 hours.


Meanwhile, Kaycie balanced her work as a dental hygienist, parenting responsibilities, and an increasingly active role in developing WIT.


John admits the process tested their communication and patience.


“We’ve learned to work together, and I’ve learned to listen to her ideas and listen to the things that she brings, which is all super valuable,” he shared.


When asked what advice he would give his younger self, John didn’t hesitate.


“Be a little more patient,” he said. “Patient with the process.”


He also emphasized persistence, continuing to move forward even when progress feels slower than expected.


For other entrepreneurs, particularly those building businesses with spouses or family members, the Bogners’ experience offers a reminder that success requires more than a shared vision.


It requires communication, flexibility, and a willingness to recognize the strengths each person brings to the table.


## Why Strong Business Relationships Matter


Although WIT Athletics was John and Kaycie’s vision, bringing it to life required the support of many people.


From builders and family members to longtime friends, fellow entrepreneurs, and financial partners, John credits a broad network for helping turn the idea into reality.


“I relied on a ton of people,” he said. “This was a collective effort from people I built relationships with and trusted.”


That collaborative approach also shaped WIT’s relationship with Landmark National Bank.


For John, having a banker who was accessible, responsive, and willing to work through complex questions made an important difference during the planning and construction process.


As the project evolved, Landmark helped John navigate financing considerations and better understand how to structure the resources available to his business.


Beyond the financial relationship, John appreciates Landmark’s commitment to local entrepreneurship.


He sees that commitment reflected in Michael Burns, who shares his interest in supporting businesses and the Dodge City community.


For business owners considering a major investment, expansion, or new venture, WIT’s experience highlights the value of finding financial partners who understand both the numbers and the people behind them.


A banking relationship can be about more than securing financing. It can also provide access to knowledgeable professionals who help entrepreneurs evaluate options, work through challenges, and make informed decisions.


## Strength in Community


For John, WIT Athletics has always been about something bigger than opening a gym.


It’s about investing in the place he calls home.


Growing up in the family beverage business, John watched his father build relationships and give back to the community. Two lessons have stayed with him throughout his career.


“Treat people like you want to be treated,” John recalled. “And take care of the people that take care of you.”


Those principles now guide the culture at WIT Athletics.


John and Kaycie want every person who walks through the doors to feel welcome, regardless of their background, experience, or fitness level.


Their children have also played a role in building the business, helping with everything from everyday operations to social media content.


For John, watching the next generation become involved is especially meaningful because it mirrors his own childhood experiences working alongside his father.


And while WIT Athletics continues to establish itself in Dodge City, John remains open to future opportunities to bring the concept to other communities.


His motivation, however, remains the same: creating something that serves people well.


That commitment to local relationships and community investment is also what makes WIT Athletics a natural fit for Landmark’s Customer Champions series. Both organizations recognize that the strength of a community is closely connected to the people and businesses willing to invest in its future.


## Doing Whatever It Takes, Together


WIT Athletics is proof that entrepreneurship rarely follows a perfectly predictable path.


Sometimes it means walking away from a familiar career. Sometimes it means reworking a business plan, listening to a different perspective, or leaning on the people around you when challenges arise.


For John and Kaycie, building WIT has required all of those things.


Their story offers an important perspective for business owners at any stage: Stay committed to your vision, but remain flexible in how you achieve it. Build relationships before you need them. And never underestimate the value of understanding the community you serve.


For Landmark National Bank, supporting entrepreneurs like John and Kaycie is about more than a single transaction. It’s about building relationships that help local businesses pursue their goals and contribute to the communities they call home.


Because doing Whatever It Takes doesn’t mean doing everything alone.


It means bringing the right people, ideas, and resources together to build something worth believing in.
